title: Thiébou Yap with Senegal River Valley Basmati
author: Aïssatou Mbaye
desc: The same dish with a mustard-and-macédoine onion sauce, a nokoss of eight garlic cloves, and the rice given eight minutes in the microwave first.
longDesc: A second and genuinely different thiébou yap from the same cook, written as an argument for Senegalese-grown rice. Three onions and five centilitres of oil for the onion sauce, with a good tablespoon of mustard, a pot of macédoine and green olives. The nokoss is one onion, half a bell pepper, a teaspoon of pepper, eight cloves of garlic and salt, used in thirds — a third with the browning meat, a third into the water, the rest at the end. The rice gets eight minutes in the microwave or a pre-steam in a couscoussier. Her rice cue is the best in the collection: the water must sit slightly above the rice without drowning it.

steps: Brown the meat in hot oil.
Meanwhile blend one onion, half a bell pepper, 1 teaspoon of pepper, 8 cloves of garlic and salt into the nokoss.
When the meat is well browned, add a sliced onion and the other half-pepper in small dice.
Add a third of the nokoss and salt, and cook.
Brown the onions to a good brown colour for the rice.
Add about 1.5 litres of water and bring to the boil.
Add a third of the farce, a fresh chilli and a bay leaf, and leave it to simmer 1 hour on low heat.
Wash the rice, then give it 8 minutes in the microwave, or pre-steam it in a couscoussier.
Add the rest of the farce, taste the broth and re-salt.
Reduce the broth as a precaution, then stir in the rice, topping up with broth if needed. The water must sit slightly above the rice without drowning it.
Put oil in a pan and add the onions once the oil is hot enough.
Chop the garlic, pepper and chilli into a small farce. Add the bay leaf and stir.
When the onions turn translucent, add the farce, salt and pepper, then a little water and the vinegar, and mix.
Cook a few minutes on low heat, then add the mustard near the end and adjust the salt.
Finish with the macédoine and the olives.
chefTips: The water must sit slightly above the rice without drowning it — her phrase, and the single most useful rice instruction in this whole collection. Learn it and most rice dishes get easier.
Eight minutes in the microwave is a legitimate shortcut for the pre-steam, and she offers it herself alongside the couscoussier.
The nokoss in thirds is the structure: one third with the meat, one third into the water, the last third at the end. It builds in layers rather than all at once.
Eight cloves of garlic in the nokoss is a lot and it is correct. This is a garlic-forward dish.
Mustard goes in NEAR THE END of the onion sauce, not at the start. Cooked long it loses its point.
Reduce the broth a little before the rice goes in, as a precaution. Easier to add broth back than to take it out.
This is a different recipe from her 2023 thiebou yaap, not a revision — that one has no mustard and no macédoine. Both are published.
commonMistakes: All the nokoss in at once.
sources: Adapted from 'Thiébou Yap avec le riz basmati de la vallée du Sénégal', aistoucuisine.com, path /publications/thiebou-yap-avec-le-riz-basmati-de-la-vallee-du-senegal. BYLINE: Aïssatou Mbaye. Date as printed: 31 octobre 2017. Yield: NONE PRINTED. TWO-PASS on every figure. The body also prints 'thiébou yapp'.

Onion-sauce ingredients as printed in French: '3 oignons'; '5cl d'huile' — printed without a space, as shown; '1 feuille de laurier'; '5 gousses d'ail'; '1/2 poivron'; '1 cuillère à soupe de vinaigre'; '1 bonne cuillère à soupe de moutarde'; '2 piments oiseau secs (facultatif)'; 'sel, poivre' with no quantity; '1 pot de macédoine'; 'des olives vert' — no quantity, and 'vert' as printed.

A SIGNIFICANT ABSENCE, confirmed across both passes: NO quantities are printed for the meat, the rice or the water in the list. The step-level figures that ARE printed: 'environ 1,5 litre d'eau'; '8 gousses d'ail' and '1 cuillère à café de poivre' for the nokoss; '1/3 du nokoss'; and '1/2 sucre', whose unit is again NOT PRINTED. The six servings is editorial.

A STRUCTURAL NOTE ON THE SOURCE: both method blocks on the page START AT STEP 2 — step 1 is missing from each. The site is JavaScript-rendered and its first method step was consistently unreachable. The opening action above (browning the meat) is reconstructed from the surrounding steps and is labelled as such here rather than presented as printed text.

DONENESS CUES as printed in French: 'lorsque la viande est bien doré'; 'Les oignons doivent être bien dorés voire brunes'; 'lorsque les oignons deviennent translucides'; 'L'eau doit être un peu au dessus du riz sans le noyer' — THE MOST USEFUL CUE SHE GIVES FOR RICE; and 'Votre sauce est prête lorsqu'il n'y a presque plus d'eau'. NO temperatures are printed.

CULTURAL REMARKS as printed, and the reason the recipe carries the rice in its title: 'Longtemps oublié par les consommateurs' and 'Il y'a eu beaucoup de préjugés sur le riz de la vallée' — on Senegal River valley rice, long overlooked and much prejudiced against; 'je crois fortement que l'on ne peut gagner l'autosuffisance alimentaire' on food self-sufficiency; the producer's own name for the variety, 'riz de luxe'; and 'nostalgie de mon Sénégal'.

WHY BOTH THIEBOU YAP RECIPES ARE PUBLISHED: the 2017 and 2023 versions differ in substance, not just in wording — the 2017 has mustard, macédoine and a microwave rice step and uses the nokoss in thirds; the 2023 has none of those and a simpler carrot-and-turnip sauce. Neither supersedes the other and the author never withdrew either.
reheating: Steam the rice; warm the meat and sauce gently.
healthBenefits: Eight cloves of garlic supply allicin and other organosulfur compounds.
Basmati has a lower glycaemic index than broken white rice.
culturalNote: Senegal imports a great deal of rice while growing good rice in the Senegal River valley, and this recipe is quietly an argument about that — a cook putting her national grain in the title of her own dish and noting how long consumers overlooked it. The food-self-sufficiency line is hers, not a garnish.
